summary: The agent didn't take Task 2. It loaded the SDD skill and made a worktree. It never ran `sdd-state register` or `next`, and it added its session line to the ledger by hand. Then it tried to claim the held Task 1, got "held", and asked me what to do. After I answered "No, the other session is still working." it stopped without claiming or working Task 2.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 5 clearly failed. The agent stopped at the held task and handed back instead of claiming the frontier task, which is exactly the behaviour this scenario tests for. Only the skill invocation (1) and no takeover (4) passed.

observations.description: The agent stopped and handed back on the held Task 1 when it should have taken the claimable Task 2. It said: "The plan's process says that when another session holds a task, I wait for you to say which tasks this session should run." Either the skill's held-task rule says to wait, or the agent misread it.

The agent never used `sdd-state register` or `sdd-state next`. It added its session line to progress.md with a hand-written `cat >> ... <<EOF` instead of using the tool's verb. That skips the tool's own bookkeeping.
It tried to claim Task 1 first, even though the user had said Task 1 was held. It doesn't seem to check which tasks are claimable before trying a claim.

The question bundled the takeover choice with a general 'what should I do' choice. A plain 'No' to takeover then led the agent to do nothing at all instead of going ahead with its own recommended option (Take Task 2).

Launch setup: the workspace trust dialog has 'No, exit' selected by default, and a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt came up even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed. Esc didn't close that prompt, so I chose 'No'.
In the earlier `sync` output, the line 'status=ok tasks=0' seems to say the plan has zero tasks, but the plan has three. It might be a count of something else, but it reads confusingly.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in session log 8bdc20cb...jsonl: "Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development". The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: Ran sdd-state register and sdd-state next; next names Task 2
criteria.evidence: The list of Bash commands in the session log has only `sdd-state sync`, `sdd-dir`, `sdd-state verify` and `sdd-state claim ... 1`. There is no `register` and no `next`. The ledger session line was written by hand: `cat >> .../progress.md <<'EOF' session 8bdc20cb-...: mode worktree on worktree-parallel-b ...`.

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with --session and worked it; ledger has 'Task 2: branch'
criteria.evidence: No `sdd-state claim ... 2` command appears in the log. The only claim was `sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 1 --session 8bdc20cb-...`, which returned `status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session` with exit=4. progress.md has no 'Task 2:' line, and claims/ contains only task-1.

I listed every Bash tool_use command with jq. The one Task 1 claim is `sdd-state claim ... 1 --session 8bdc...` with no --takeover. grep finds '--takeover' 4 times in the log, but those matches come from places that aren't Bash commands. One I saw is the AskUserQuestion option text "(--takeover)". I assume the others are skill text but didn't check.

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at held Task 1 before taking Task 2
criteria.evidence: Right after the held result for Task 1, the agent asked (AskUserQuestion) "What should this session do?" with options Take Task 2 / Take Tasks 2 and 3 / Take over Task 1 / Wait. I answered "No, the other session is still working." It then handed back: "I'm not taking over Task 1, and I haven't started anything else... If you want this session to take Task 2, or Tasks 2 and 3, say so." It never claimed Task 2.
